subject.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path

question: Should Skill Workshop chat authoring and lifecycle approval require owner/admin identity, and if so should the owner gate cover proposal creation as well as apply/reject/quarantine approval?
rationale: The current implementation crosses a workspace-write security boundary, but the durable product choice is whether drafting pending proposals remains a normal authorized-user capability or becomes owner-only like live skill/plugin mutation.

options.title: Gate live writes and approvals
options.body: Require owner or `operator.admin` for `skill_workshop` lifecycle actions and `/approve` decisions that resolve Skill Workshop plugin approvals, while separately evaluating whether pending proposal creation stays available to authorized senders.

options.title: Gate all Skill Workshop chat authoring
options.body: Require owner or `operator.admin` for `/learn` and all `skill_workshop` mutating actions, making chat Skill Workshop match the Gateway admin proposal API boundary.

options.title: Keep same-chat approval
options.body: Document and accept that authorized non-owner chat participants may create and apply workspace skills through approval prompts, which preserves current behavior but leaves the reported boundary open.

recommendation.title: Gate live writes and approvals
recommendation.body: Require owner or `operator.admin` for `skill_workshop` lifecycle actions and `/approve` decisions that resolve Skill Workshop plugin approvals, while separately evaluating whether pending proposal creation stays available to authorized senders.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced `/learn` and has the clearest recent history across this command and Skill Workshop policy surface.
